title: "System Boundary and Carrier-Cost Metrics"
completion: 70
readiness: partially_implementable

## Role in the Model

This page defines what each architecture delivers, which costs enter the model
result and how those costs are normalized. Component pages calculate the
underlying physical quantities, energy flows and costs.

## Tier 1 Delivery Boundary

The model currently reports carrier-specific Tier 1 products:

| Architecture | Delivery endpoint | Delivered quantity |
|---|---|---|
| Electricity export | Defined onshore electrical delivery point after onshore conversion | Electrical energy |
| Centralised hydrogen | Defined onshore hydrogen delivery point after offshore production, compression and export | Hydrogen mass and HHV energy |
| Decentralised hydrogen | Defined onshore hydrogen delivery point after turbine-level production, collection, compression and export | Hydrogen mass and HHV energy |

Storage, reconversion, downstream distribution, demand matching and end use are
outside the Tier 1 boundary. They may be added only through a future Tier 2
scenario.

EUR/MWh-electricity and EUR/MWh-H2-HHV therefore describe different delivered
carrier products. They may be displayed side by side, but they must not be
labelled as equivalent end-use prices or used to claim a like-for-like carrier
ranking.

## Cost Boundary

The model distinguishes initial installed CAPEX from the lifecycle capital
basis used for annualization.

| Cost category | Treatment and owner |
|---|---|
| Component supply CAPEX | Owned by the component page |
| Offshore installation CAPEX | Owned by the applicable installation page |
| Onshore equipment and connection CAPEX | Owned by the applicable component page |
| Annual OPEX | Owned by the component page on a non-overlapping scope |
| Material short-life replacement | Owned by the component page; counted only when replacement is required within 25 years |
| Decommissioning | Shared calculation on the financial page: 80% of total offshore installation CAPEX |
| Commissioning | Owned once by the applicable installation/component interface |
| Development and shared engineering | Shared project-cost field; currently unresolved |
| Insurance and owner contingency | Shared project-cost field; currently unresolved |
| Construction finance, taxes and financing fees | Excluded by the approved simple-CRF convention |
| Residual value | Zero under the 25-year project convention |

Development, shared engineering, insurance and owner contingency are not
silently zero. Until they are parameterized, a complete total-system cost
returns **not parameterized**. Explicitly bounded component or modelled-cost
subtotals may still be reported, but they must not be called total system cost.

## Capital-Intensity Outputs

Let $P_{\mathrm{wind,rated}}$ be installed wind-turbine rated capacity in kW.

Initial installed capital intensity is:

$$
c_{\mathrm{initial}}
=
\frac{C_{\mathrm{initial}}}
{P_{\mathrm{wind,rated}}},
$$

where $c_{\mathrm{initial}}$ has units EUR~2025~/kW-wind.

The lifecycle capital basis may also be reported separately:

$$
c_{\mathrm{lifecycle}}
=
\frac{C_{\mathrm{lifecycle\ capital}}}
{P_{\mathrm{wind,rated}}}.
$$

The label must state whether replacement and decommissioning are included.
Neither metric may be normalized by electrolyser, converter, pipeline or export
capacity when it is presented as the cross-architecture wind-capacity result.

## Annual Carrier-Cost Outputs

For electricity:

$$
LC_{\mathrm{electricity}}
=
\frac{C_{\mathrm{annual,electricity}}}
{E_{\mathrm{electricity,onshore}}},
$$

with numerator in EUR~2025~/year, denominator in
MWh-electricity/year and result in EUR~2025~/MWh-electricity.

For hydrogen:

$$
LC_{\mathrm{H2,HHV}}
=
\frac{C_{\mathrm{annual,H2}}}
{E_{\mathrm{H2,onshore,HHV}}},
$$

with result in EUR~2025~/MWh-H2-HHV.

Hydrogen cost per kilogram is derived from the same result:

$$
LC_{\mathrm{H2,kg}}
=
LC_{\mathrm{H2,HHV}}
\frac{HHV_{\mathrm{H2}}}{1000},
$$

where $HHV_{\mathrm{H2}}$ is in kWh/kg. At 39.4 kWh/kg, the conversion
factor is 0.0394 MWh/kg.

The financial numerator is calculated on
[Financial and Price-Basis Assumptions](financial_and_price_basis.qmd).
Delivered-energy accounting is defined on
[Energy and Availability](energy_availability_and_annualisation.qmd).
